newsitem.title: INDIA: HIGHLIGHTS-RBI credit policy for second half 96/97.
newsitem.headline: HIGHLIGHTS-RBI credit policy for second half 96/97.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy for second half 1996/97 (April-March) announced on Saturday:
** CRR (cash reserve ratios held by banks) cut to 10 percent
from 12 percent in four stages of 50 basis points each,
effective October 26, November 9, January 4, 1997 and
January 18.
** Export credit refinance of 20 percent of outstanding
export credit eligible for refinance (against 45 percent
at present) upto the level of such credit outstanding on
February 16, 1996 plus 100 percent of increase in
eligible outstanding export credit over the February 16
figure.
** Export credit targets increased to 12 percent of net bank
credit from 10 percent.
** Deposit interest rate cap for maturities upto one year
reduced to 10 percent per annum from 11 percent.
** Interest rates on post-shipment rupee export credit
beyond 90 days and upto six months capped at 15 percent
per annum against no ceiling.
** Banks should announce maximum spreads over prime lending
rate for all advances other than consumer credit.
** Bank advances against sugar, oilseeds and oils, cotton,
pulses and coarse grains exempt from selective credit
controls.
** Banks allowed to lend in foreign currencies from FCNR(B)
deposits.
** Participating banks allowed to frame their own rules for
consortium lending.
** Loan component of working capital credit disbursed by
banks increased to 75 percent from 60 percent for
borrowers of 200 million rupees and above and to 60
percent from 40 percent for borrowers of 100 million
rupees to 200 million rupees.
** Commercial paper limits need not be carved out of cash
credit component of working capital loans.
** Banks allowed to purchase shares and debentures in
secondary market.
